sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Mason, Ohio?
sections.html:
Mason homeowners have three practical paths: hire an agent, handle the sale alone, or accept an as-is cash purchase. The county work after a contract is the same for all three, and it runs through Warren County's auditor and recorder.

Speed is the main trade. A traditional listing can attract many buyers, yet it also invites inspection credits, staging effort and weeks of showings. A direct cash sale skips most of that and lets you pick a closing date.

  • With an agent, you pay a commission and work through repair requests.
  • On your own, you keep that commission and take on every task yourself.
  • With a cash buyer, you accept a negotiated price in return for certainty and a short timeline.

sections.h2: What do the numbers show about Mason homes and households?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists Mason's median owner-occupied home value at $426,200 for 2020-2024, with 80.1 percent of homes lived in by their owners. The Census Bureau puts July 1, 2025 population at 35,834, which is 3.0 percent above the 2020 base.

QuickFacts lists median household income at $125,401 and median gross rent at $1,760. Of residents aged 25 and over, 60.4 percent hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and 17.1 percent of residents were born outside the United States. Mason has 13,502 households with 2.60 people each.

The city covers about 19 square miles, and the Little Miami River forms a short stretch of its border.

sections.h2: How did Mason grow into a Warren County city?
sections.html:
Mason began as farmland: in 1803 William Mason paid $1,700 at auction for 640 acres in what is now downtown, and in 1815 he platted 16 lots and named the village Palmyra. Postal confusion with another Ohio Palmyra led to the name Mason in 1835.

For well over a century it stayed small. Main Street was paved in 1923, and in 1970, a year before Mason incorporated as a city, fewer than 5,700 people lived there. By the 2020 census the count was 34,792, and in 1997 the city separated from Deerfield Township to form a paper township named Mason Township.

One landmark from the early years still shapes the skyline: the WLW radio tower on Tylersville Road, built in 1928.

sections.h2: Which employers and attractions affect Mason buyers?
sections.html:
Corporate employers anchor the local economy. Cintas is headquartered in Mason, along with the Procter & Gamble Mason Business Center and the headquarters of Luxottica Retail, and more than 90 companies operate headquarters or manufacturing sites across the city's 24 commerce parks.

Kings Island amusement park and the Lindner Family Tennis Center, home of the Cincinnati Open, also sit in Mason. The city is about 22 miles north of downtown Cincinnati, and Sinclair Community College runs a 75-acre campus near I-71.

  • Seven city parks cover about 300 acres, with lakes, trails and ball fields.
  • The Mason Community Center, opened in 2003, covers 199,000 square feet with two pools and a senior center.
  • The Mason Municipal Center houses the municipal court, police and fire departments.

Mason City Schools serves the city with five public schools: Mason Early Childhood Center for pre-K through second grade, Mason Elementary for grades 3 and 4, Mason Intermediate for grades 5 and 6, Mason Middle for grades 7 and 8, and William Mason High School.

The last of these buildings to open was Mason Elementary, in 2019. Families often ask about the district before anything else, so put the school names on your listing sheet or give them to a cash buyer who plans to resell.

sections.h2: What does a deed transfer cost in Warren County?
sections.html:
Warren County's auditor lists a mandatory conveyance fee of $1.00 per thousand dollars of the purchase price and a county transfer tax of $2.00 per thousand, which together make $3.00. A transfer fee of $0.50 per parcel is added, and pennies in the total are rounded up to the next ten cents.

Warren County auditor charges when a deed is transferred
ChargeAmount printedBasis
Conveyance fee$1.00 per $1,000 of priceState law, mandatory
Transfer tax$2.00 per $1,000 of pricePermissive county levy under ORC 322.02
Combined per $1,000$3.00Pennies rounded up to next 10 cents
Transfer fee$0.50 per parcelPer appraisal card if more than one taxing district

Source: Warren County Auditor, Real Property Transfers and Conveyances page.

The seller pays these charges at the time the deed is presented, and the auditor endorses the deed once they are paid.

sections.h2: What paperwork does Warren County require on a Mason deed?
sections.html:
Warren County requires a properly completed statement of value (DTE Form 100) or an exemption statement (DTE Form 100EX) with every deed, and the fees are payable to the Warren County Auditor. Before the deed reaches the auditor, the county map department must approve and initial it.

  • The grantor's name must read the way the grantor took title on the previous deed.
  • The prior deed reference of record must appear on the new deed.
  • If the land is in the farm-use valuation program now or was last year, DTE Form 102 must accompany the deed.
  • The grantor signs every Ohio deed, and a notary must acknowledge it.

Exemption reasons (b), (g) and (m) on the 100EX form require a notarized affidavit explaining why no money changed hands.

sections.h2: Which Mason projects need permits before closing?
sections.html:
Mason's Engineering, Building and Planning Department handles permits through an online portal, and it can be reached at 513.229.8520. Applications cover residential building and electric work, decks, pools and spas, fences, solar, demolition, retaining walls, sewer tap-ins and signs, as well as zoning certificates.

Ask the department about any open permits or completed work without a final inspection. Unfinished permits can stall a conventional sale, and a cash buyer will usually discount for them. A zoning certificate also answers whether a property is zoned for the use a buyer has in mind.

sections.h2: What should a Mason rental owner file after a sale?
sections.html:
Ohio law requires owners of residential rental property to register contact details with the county auditor and to update them within 60 days after a change (Ohio Revised Code 5323.02). A new owner of a Mason rental should expect that filing to follow the deed.

If you are selling a rented house, agree in the contract on who handles deposits, the lease and move-out dates, and keep copies of what you give the buyer.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer suit a Mason seller?
sections.html:
Some Mason sellers want a short timeline instead of a long listing, and a cash sale can suit them. Examples include:

  • Owners relocating for a job on a deadline.
  • Heirs who have inherited a house and live elsewhere.
  • Sellers of a home that needs work that would cost more than they want to spend.

Request the offer in writing, and compare it with a realistic net from listing.

faqs.q: Who pays Warren County's deed fees on a Mason sale?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, pays them when the deed is presented to the auditor. Ohio Revised Code 319.202 places the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax on the grantor.

faqs.q: Does the Mason seller need to sign anything before the deed is accepted?
faqs.a: Yes. The grantor signs the deed, and the signing must be acknowledged before a notary or another official named in Ohio Revised Code 5301.01. Warren County also asks that the grantor's name match the previous deed.

faqs.q: Is a property disclosure form required in Mason?
faqs.a: For a house with one to four dwelling units, yes, unless an exception applies. The form must be completed and handed to the buyer, and exceptions include estate transfers and relatives in the direct line.

faqs.q: What is the DTE 100EX form used for?
faqs.a: It states why a transfer is exempt from the conveyance fee. The buyer or the buyer's representative completes it, picks one of the listed reasons, and signs and dates it.

faqs.q: Where do I call about permits in Mason?
faqs.a: Call the city's Engineering, Building and Planning Department at 513.229.8520. Applications and permit fees are handled through the city's online permit portal.
